source.text: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: No therefore now condemnation to the [ones] in Christ Jesus;

en.L: So now [there is] no condemnation for those in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: So then, those who are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus now face no sentence of condemnation.
en.R: So now God does not condemn those who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. No sentence of punishment hangs over them.

es.L: Por tanto, ahora no [hay] condenación alguna para los [que están] en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.B: Así pues, los que están en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} ya no enfrentan ninguna sentencia de condenación.
es.R: Así que ahora Dios no condena a los que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. Ya no pesa sobre ellos ninguna sentencia de castigo.

fr.L: Donc maintenant, [il n’y a] aucune condamnation pour ceux [qui sont] {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, ceux qui sont {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus ne sont plus maintenant sous le coup d’aucune condamnation.
fr.R: Maintenant, Dieu ne condamne donc pas ceux qui appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Aucune sentence de punition ne pèse sur eux.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sasa hakuna kuhukumiwa kwa wale walio katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Basi sasa, wale walio katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu hawakabiliwi na hukumu yoyote ya kuadhibiwa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sasa Mungu hawahukumu wale walio wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Hakuna adhabu inayowangoja.

decisions.choice: condemnation: the sentence passed on the guilty, and the penalty it carries
decisions.reason: katakrima is a law-court word: the judge's verdict against someone and the punishment that follows. Paul used it in 5:16 and 5:18, where Adam's trespass led to condemnation for all. Here that verdict is gone for those in Christ.

decisions.choice: "so now": a conclusion, and a new time
alternatives: "now" as only "at this point in the argument"
decisions.reason: ara draws the conclusion of what Paul has said since 5:12, and especially of 7:25. "Now" is the time that began with Christ, as in 3:21 ("but now") and 5:9: what was true of life under sin is no longer true.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus: joined to him, sharing his death and life
decisions.reason: Paul has said that believers were baptized into Christ, died with him and live with him (6:3-11). Being "in" him is that union, and the verdict that falls on him now falls on them.

decisions.choice: the verse ends at "in Christ Jesus"
alternatives: adds "who walk not according to the flesh" (and, in later copies, "but according to the Spirit")
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts end the verse here. Later copies add words from verse 4, so that the verse no longer says that freedom from condemnation depends on being in Christ alone; the longer form is in the King James Version. The SBLGNT has the short text. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: face no sentence of condemnation (B); God does not condemn them, no sentence of punishment (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the word is a judge's sentence (m1). Readable names God as the judge, since he alone passes this sentence (verse 33).

decisions.choice: who belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ Jesus" as belonging to him (m3).

decisions.choice: "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ"; "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" elsewhere
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for Paul's "in Christ" covers the preposition, with the familiar "en Christ" as the default. Elsewhere the article stays outside the span, since "le Christ" and "le Messie" both read naturally; Literal adds it without brackets.

decisions.choice: ne sont plus sous le coup d’aucune condamnation
alternatives: n’ont plus à craindre aucune sentence
decisions.reason: "Être sous le coup d’une condamnation" is the French legal phrase for a sentence that hangs over someone, which is what the English "face no sentence" brings out (m1).

decisions.choice: kuhukumiwa (L); hukumu ... ya kuadhibiwa (B); Mungu hawahukumu, hakuna adhabu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the sentence passed on the guilty together with the penalty it carries (m1). "Hukumu" alone is any judgment or verdict, so Literal uses the passive verb "kuhukumiwa" (being condemned), Balanced names the penalty ("hukumu ya kuadhibiwa"), and Readable splits the two, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου.

records.literal_gloss: The for law of the Spirit of the life in Christ Jesus set free you from the law of the sin and of the death.

en.L: For the law of the Spirit of life in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus set you free from the law of sin and of death.
en.B: For in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus the law of the Spirit who gives life has freed you from the law of sin and death.
en.R: The Spirit gives life to everyone who is joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. And the Spirit's power has set you free from the power of sin, which leads to death.

es.L: Porque la ley del Espíritu de la vida en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} te liberó de la ley del pecado y de la muerte.
es.B: Porque en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} la ley del Espíritu que da vida te ha hecho libre de la ley del pecado y de la muerte.
es.R: El Espíritu da vida a todos los que están unidos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. Y el poder del Espíritu te ha liberado del poder del pecado, que lleva a la muerte.

fr.L: Car la loi de l’Esprit de la vie {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus t’a libéré de la loi du péché et de la mort.
fr.B: Car, {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, la loi de l’Esprit qui donne la vie t’a libéré de la loi du péché et de la mort.
fr.R: L’Esprit donne la vie à tous ceux qui sont unis au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Et la puissance de l’Esprit t’a libéré de la puissance du péché, qui mène à la mort.

sw.L: Kwa maana sheria ya Roho wa uzima katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu ilikuweka huru mbali na sheria ya dhambi na ya kifo.
sw.B: Kwa maana katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, sheria ya Roho anayetoa uzima imekuweka huru kutoka kwa sheria ya dhambi na kifo.
sw.R: Roho humpa uzima kila mtu aliyeunganishwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Na nguvu ya Roho imekuweka huru kutoka kwa nguvu ya dhambi, inayoleta kifo.

decisions.choice: law: here a ruling power or order, the Spirit's against sin's
alternatives: the law of Moses in both places: the same law, used by the Spirit or by sin
decisions.reason: Paul has just spoken of "another law" at work in his body, "the law of sin" (7:21-23). Here he sets the rule of the Spirit against that rule of sin. Some read both phrases as the law of Moses, which sin used to bring death (7:10-11) and which the Spirit now fulfills (verse 4); the wording allows that too.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of life: the Spirit who gives life
alternatives: "the spirit of life" as a quality, a living spirit
decisions.reason: Paul names the Spirit as the one who gives life in verses 10-11, against sin which leads to death.

decisions.choice: "in Christ Jesus" goes with the whole saying: the Spirit sets free those joined to Christ
alternatives: goes only with "life": the life that is in Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between "life" and "set free" and may go with either. Both say that the freedom and the life come in union with Christ (verse 1), so the levels keep it close to both.

decisions.choice: "you" (singular)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have "you" in the singular, Paul speaking to each reader in turn; some have "me", continuing chapter 7, and a few "us". The SBLGNT has "you". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the Spirit's power; the power of sin
alternatives: the Spirit's law; the law of sin
decisions.reason: Readable says "power" for the sense the meaning decision prefers (m1), so a new reader does not think of a written law code; the decision is marked uncertain for reviewers.

decisions.choice: te (tú), no setting
decisions.reason: The Greek "you" here is singular (m4): Paul speaks to each reader. Spanish keeps the singular "te", which needs no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: la loi, lowercase, here; la Loi for the Law of Moses (8:3, 8:4, 8:7)
decisions.reason: Here the word means a ruling power or order, the Spirit's set against sin's (m1), so French writes it lowercase, as the style guide does for law as a principle (7:23). The capital is kept for the Law of Moses, which is weak through the flesh in the next verse.

decisions.choice: t’a libéré ("tu", singular)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular (m4), and French follows the Greek number: Paul turns to the single reader, as he does in 2:1 and 7:7-25.

decisions.choice: -ku- (ilikuweka huru, imekuweka huru)
decisions.reason: The Greek "you" is singular (m4), and Swahili keeps the singular object marker "-ku-" at every level.

decisions.choice: kifo
decisions.reason: For death through this chapter Swahili uses "kifo", the plain everyday word, at every level. "Mauti" is the older word familiar from church reading; it means the same, and a reviewer may prefer it at Literal.

source.text: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου, ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός, ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα·

records.literal_gloss: The for impossible [thing] of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, the God the of himself Son having sent in likeness of flesh of sin and concerning sin condemned the sin in the flesh, \v 4 so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, the [ones] not according to flesh walking but according to Spirit;

en.L: For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God [did]: sending {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son in [the] likeness of flesh of sin, and for sin, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} condemned sin in the flesh, \v 4 so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to [the] flesh but according to [the] Spirit.
en.B: The law was powerless, since the flesh had left it weak. So God acted. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, as an offering for sin, and in the flesh {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed sentence on sin. \v 4 He did this so that the law's righteous requirement would be fully met in us, who conduct our lives by the Spirit and not by the flesh.
en.R: The law could not do this, because our sinful selves were too weak to keep it. But God did it. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Son as a real human being, with a body like the bodies of sinful people. God sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be an offering for sin. In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} human body God judged sin and condemned it. \v 4 God did this so that what the law rightly requires would come true in us. Now we do not follow our sinful selves. We follow the Spirit.

es.L: Porque lo imposible para la ley, en cuanto que era débil por la carne, Dios [lo hizo]: enviando a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Hijo en [la] semejanza de [la] carne de pecado, y por el pecado, condenó el pecado en la carne, \v 4 para que la justa exigencia de la ley se cumpliera en nosotros, que no andamos según [la] carne sino según [el] Espíritu.
es.B: La ley no tenía poder, porque la carne la había dejado débil. Por eso actuó Dios. Envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Hijo en semejanza de carne pecadora, como ofrenda por el pecado, y en la carne dictó sentencia contra el pecado. \v 4 Lo hizo para que la justa exigencia de la ley se cumpliera plenamente en nosotros, que llevamos nuestra vida guiados por el Espíritu y no por la carne.
es.R: La ley no podía hacer esto, porque nuestro yo pecador era demasiado débil para cumplirla. Pero Dios lo hizo. Envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Hijo como un verdadero ser humano, con un cuerpo como el de la gente pecadora. Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió para ser una ofrenda por el pecado. En {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo humano, Dios juzgó al pecado y lo condenó. \v 4 Dios hizo esto para que lo que la ley justamente exige se hiciera realidad en nosotros. Ahora no vivimos según lo que quiere nuestro yo pecador. Vivimos guiados por el Espíritu.

fr.L: Car ce qui était impossible à la Loi, en ce qu’elle était faible à cause de la chair, Dieu [l’a fait] : en envoyant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Fils dans la ressemblance d’une chair de péché, et pour le péché, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a condamné le péché dans la chair, \v 4 afin que la juste exigence de la Loi soit accomplie en nous, qui marchons non selon la chair mais selon l’Esprit.
fr.B: La Loi était impuissante, car la chair l’avait rendue faible. Alors Dieu a agi. Il a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Fils, qui a pris une chair pareille à notre chair pécheresse, comme sacrifice pour le péché, et dans cette chair {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a prononcé la sentence contre le péché. \v 4 Il l’a fait pour que la juste exigence de la Loi soit pleinement accomplie en nous, qui menons notre vie selon l’Esprit et non selon la chair.
fr.R: La Loi ne pouvait pas faire cela, parce que notre nature pécheresse était trop faible pour l’observer. Mais Dieu l’a fait. Il a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Fils comme un véritable être humain, avec un corps semblable à celui des pécheurs. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé pour être un sacrifice pour le péché. Dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps humain, Dieu a jugé le péché et l’a condamné. \v 4 Dieu a fait cela pour que ce que la Loi demande à juste titre se réalise en nous. Maintenant, nous ne suivons plus notre nature pécheresse. Nous suivons l’Esprit.

sw.L: Kwa maana kile ambacho sheria haikuweza, kwa kuwa ilikuwa dhaifu kwa sababu ya mwili, Mungu [alikifanya]: akimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe kwa sura ya mwili wa dhambi, na kwa ajili ya dhambi, aliihukumu dhambi ndani ya mwili, \v 4 ili matakwa ya haki ya sheria yatimizwe ndani yetu, sisi tusiotembea kwa kadiri ya mwili bali kwa kadiri ya Roho.
sw.B: Sheria haikuwa na uwezo, kwa kuwa asili ya dhambi iliidhoofisha. Kwa hiyo Mungu alitenda. Alimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe akiwa na mfano wa mwili wenye dhambi, kama sadaka kwa ajili ya dhambi, na katika mwili huo akaitolea dhambi hukumu. \v 4 Alifanya hivyo ili matakwa ya haki ya sheria yatimizwe kikamilifu ndani yetu, sisi tunaoishi tukiongozwa na Roho, wala si na asili ya dhambi.
sw.R: Sheria haikuweza kufanya hivyo, kwa sababu asili yetu ya dhambi ilikuwa dhaifu mno kuweza kuitii. Lakini Mungu alifanya hivyo. Alimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe kama mwanadamu halisi, mwenye mwili kama miili ya watu wenye dhambi. Mungu alimtuma ili awe sadaka kwa ajili ya dhambi. Katika mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kibinadamu Mungu aliihukumu dhambi na kuitia hatiani. \v 4 Mungu alifanya hivyo ili yale ambayo sheria inadai kwa haki yatimie ndani yetu. Sasa hatufuati tena asili yetu ya dhambi. Tunamfuata Roho.

decisions.choice: what the law could not do, God did
alternatives: "the law's weakness" as the object of "condemned"
decisions.reason: The sentence opens with "the impossible thing of the law" and never gives it a verb of its own; Paul breaks off and says what God did instead. The thing the law could not do is what verse 2 has just said: set people free from sin and death.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature, weak and under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11). The law was good (7:12), but it could not change people whose flesh was ruled by sin.

decisions.choice: in the likeness of sinful flesh: truly human, yet not himself sinful
decisions.reason: homoiōma ("likeness") lets Paul say two things at once. The Son came in real human flesh, the flesh in which sin rules in everyone else; yet he did not sin (2 Corinthians 5:21). Paul uses the same word in Philippians 2:7.

decisions.choice: for sin: as a sin offering
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament "for sin" is the regular name for the sin offering (Leviticus 4-5, 16; Isaiah 53:10). God sent the Son to be the sacrifice that deals with sin.

decisions.choice: condemned sin in the flesh: in the Son's own human nature, where sin was judged
decisions.reason: God passed sentence on sin in the very flesh where it had ruled. Because "the flesh" follows the Son coming "in the likeness of sinful flesh", it most naturally means his flesh, put to death on the cross; sin's condemnation fell there, and so not on those in Christ (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the righteous requirement is fulfilled in us: God brings it about
alternatives: "fulfilled by us" through our own effort
decisions.reason: dikaiōma is what the law rightly requires. The verb is passive and the phrase is "in us", not "by us": God's work in Christ and the Spirit bring about what the law asked for. Those in whom this happens are those who live by the Spirit.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: peripateō ("walk") is the usual biblical word for how a person lives, as in 6:4 and 13:13.

decisions.choice: the sentence is broken into four
decisions.reason: The Greek runs on from verse 3 into verse 4 and leaves its first phrase without a verb (m1). Balanced finishes that thought first, "The law was powerless", and then tells what God did in short sentences.

decisions.choice: our sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m2), as in Galatians 5 and Romans 13:14.

decisions.choice: as a real human being, with a body like the bodies of sinful people; in his human body
decisions.reason: Readable explains "likeness of sinful flesh" (m3) and "in the flesh" (m5) in plain words.

decisions.choice: conduct our lives
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the picture of walking means (m7).

decisions.choice: carne (L, B); yo pecador (R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the chapter. Where the flesh is human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit (m2), Literal and Balanced keep "carne", as the English keeps "flesh" and as Galatians 5 and Romans 13:14 do, and Readable says "yo pecador" (sinful self). Where it is the Son's own human nature ("semejanza de carne pecadora", "condenó el pecado en la carne", m3, m5), Readable says "un verdadero ser humano" and "cuerpo humano", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la chair (L, B); notre nature pécheresse (R) (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Paul: "chair" is kept at Literal and Balanced so the reader can follow the word through the chapter, where it is set against the Spirit. Readable gives the sense the meaning decision names, human nature under sin's sway (m2), as the English "our sinful selves" does; "la nature humaine" alone would not say that it is sinful.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" and elided "l’" included
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God carries the span where the English "he" does, and also where French needs a pronoun the English lacks ("Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé", Readable). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital ("Il a envoyé").

decisions.choice: mwili (L); asili ya dhambi (B, R); mwili where the Son's human nature is meant
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the chapter. Literal keeps "mwili" for the flesh throughout. Where the flesh is human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit (m2; 8:3-9, 8:12-13), Balanced and Readable say "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature), as Galatians 5 and Romans 13:14 do, because "mwili" would be heard as the body and its appetites only. Where the flesh is the Son's own human nature ("mfano wa mwili wenye dhambi", "katika mwili huo", m3, m5), every level keeps "mwili", since there it is plain human life, not sinful nature.

decisions.choice: tusiotembea kwa kadiri ya (L); tunaoishi tukiongozwa na Roho (B)
decisions.reason: Walking is the biblical picture for how one lives (m7). Literal keeps "kutembea", as Galatians 5:16 does; Balanced says "live, led by the Spirit", as there, where the English Balanced says "conduct our lives".

source.text: οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν, οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος.

records.literal_gloss: The [ones] for according to flesh being the [things] of the flesh set mind on, the [ones] but according to Spirit the [things] of the Spirit.

en.L: For those who are according to [the] flesh set [their] minds on the things of the flesh, but those [who are] according to [the] Spirit, on the things of the Spirit.
en.B: Those who are under the rule of the flesh have their minds fixed on the concerns of the flesh, but those under the rule of the Spirit, on the concerns of the Spirit.
en.R: People who live by their sinful selves think only about what their sinful selves want. But people who live by the Spirit think about what the Spirit wants.

es.L: Porque los que son según [la] carne ponen la mente en las cosas de la carne, pero los [que son] según [el] Espíritu, en las cosas del Espíritu.
es.B: Los que están bajo el dominio de la carne tienen la mente puesta en lo que interesa a la carne, pero los que están bajo el dominio del Espíritu, en lo que interesa al Espíritu.
es.R: Las personas que viven según su yo pecador solo piensan en lo que su yo pecador quiere. Pero las que viven según el Espíritu piensan en lo que el Espíritu quiere.

fr.L: Car ceux qui sont selon la chair ont la pensée tournée vers les choses de la chair, mais ceux [qui sont] selon l’Esprit, vers les choses de l’Esprit.
fr.B: Ceux qui vivent sous le règne de la chair ont les pensées fixées sur ce qui intéresse la chair, mais ceux qui vivent sous le règne de l’Esprit, sur ce qui intéresse l’Esprit.
fr.R: Les gens qui vivent selon leur nature pécheresse ne pensent qu’à ce que veut cette nature. Mais ceux qui vivent selon l’Esprit pensent à ce que veut l’Esprit.

sw.L: Kwa maana wale walio kwa kadiri ya mwili huweka nia zao katika mambo ya mwili, lakini wale [walio] kwa kadiri ya Roho, katika mambo ya Roho.
sw.B: Wale walio chini ya utawala wa asili ya dhambi huelekeza mawazo yao kwenye mambo ya asili ya dhambi, lakini wale walio chini ya utawala wa Roho, kwenye mambo ya Roho.
sw.R: Watu wanaoishi kwa kufuata asili yao ya dhambi hufikiri tu juu ya yale ambayo asili yao ya dhambi inataka. Lakini watu wanaoishi kwa kufuata Roho hufikiri juu ya yale ambayo Roho anataka.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: set the mind on: the whole bent of thought, will and desire
alternatives: think about, as a passing thought
decisions.reason: phroneō is not only thinking but what a person is set on and lives for, as in Philippians 3:19 ("their minds set on earthly things").

decisions.choice: being according to the flesh: having one's existence shaped and ruled by it
decisions.reason: Paul describes two kinds of people, those whose life is ruled by the flesh and those ruled by the Spirit. The second half of the verse leaves out the verbs, which carry over from the first.

decisions.choice: under the rule of
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "being according to" means (m3).

decisions.choice: their sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: chini ya utawala wa asili ya dhambi / wa Roho
alternatives: kwa kadiri ya asili ya dhambi
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced says "under the rule of", Swahili Balanced says "chini ya utawala wa", and keeps it where the Greek says "in the flesh" (verses 8-9), since both phrases name one way of existing with its ruling power (m3; 8:9 m2). Roho takes personal agreement ("Roho anataka"), never the agreement of a thing.

source.text: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη·

records.literal_gloss: The for mindset of the flesh death, the but mindset of the Spirit life and peace;

en.L: For the mindset of the flesh [is] death, but the mindset of the Spirit [is] life and peace.
en.B: The outlook of the flesh means death, but the outlook of the Spirit means life and peace.
en.R: When the sinful self is in charge of what you think about, the end is death. When the Spirit is in charge, there is life and peace.

es.L: Porque la mentalidad de la carne [es] muerte, pero la mentalidad del Espíritu [es] vida y paz.
es.B: La manera de pensar de la carne significa muerte, pero la manera de pensar del Espíritu significa vida y paz.
es.R: Cuando el yo pecador manda en lo que uno piensa, el final es la muerte. Cuando el Espíritu manda, hay vida y paz.

fr.L: Car la pensée de la chair [est] la mort, mais la pensée de l’Esprit [est] la vie et la paix.
fr.B: L’orientation de la chair, c’est la mort, mais l’orientation de l’Esprit, c’est la vie et la paix.
fr.R: Quand c’est notre nature pécheresse qui dirige nos pensées, cela finit par la mort. Quand c’est l’Esprit qui les dirige, il y a la vie et la paix.

sw.L: Kwa maana fikira za mwili [ni] kifo, lakini fikira za Roho [ni] uzima na amani.
sw.B: Mtazamo wa asili ya dhambi unaleta kifo, lakini mtazamo wa Roho unaleta uzima na amani.
sw.R: Asili ya dhambi ikitawala mawazo ya mtu, mwisho wake ni kifo. Roho akitawala, kuna uzima na amani.

decisions.choice: mindset: the way of thinking and wanting that belongs to the flesh or to the Spirit
alternatives: the mind as a part of a person
decisions.reason: phronēma is the noun from the verb of verse 5: a settled way of thinking and desiring.

decisions.choice: death, life and peace: separation from God, and life with him
alternatives: physical death and long life only
decisions.reason: Death here is more than the end of the body: it is the wages of sin (6:23), being cut off from God now and at the end. Life is the life of the age to come, already begun (verse 10), and peace is peace with God (5:1) and the wholeness that follows from it.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: outlook
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "outlook" for a settled way of thinking and wanting (m1).

decisions.choice: when the sinful self is in charge of what you think about
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means (m3) and turns "the mindset of" into a plain clause.

decisions.choice: mentalidad (L); manera de pensar (B); lo que uno piensa (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the whole way of thinking and wanting that belongs to the flesh or to the Spirit (m1). "Mentalidad" and "manera de pensar" say that in current Spanish. Readable uses the impersonal "uno" for the English Readable's general "you", so it needs no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: la pensée (L); l’orientation (B), also in 8:7
decisions.reason: The word is a settled way of thinking and wanting (m1). "Orientation" says the direction of the whole person, as the English "outlook" does; Literal keeps the word nearest the Greek verb "to think".

decisions.choice: fikira (L); mtazamo (B)
decisions.reason: The word is the whole bent of thinking and wanting (m1). "Fikira" (ways of thinking) keeps the link with "thinking" in verse 5; Balanced says "mtazamo" (outlook), as the English Balanced does. "Nia" (intention) would narrow it to the will.

source.text: διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν, τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται, οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται·

records.literal_gloss: Because the mindset of the flesh hostility toward God, to the for law of the God not it submits, not even for it is able;

en.L: Because the mindset of the flesh [is] hostility toward God, for it does not submit to the law of God, nor indeed is it able [to].
en.B: That is because the outlook of the flesh is at war with God. It does not bow to God's law, and in fact it is not able to.
en.R: The sinful self is God's enemy. It refuses to obey God's law, and it could never obey it.

es.L: Porque la mentalidad de la carne [es] hostilidad hacia Dios, pues no se sujeta a la ley de Dios, y ni siquiera puede [hacerlo].
es.B: Eso es porque la manera de pensar de la carne está en guerra con Dios. No se somete a la ley de Dios, y de hecho no es capaz de hacerlo.
es.R: El yo pecador es enemigo de Dios. Se niega a obedecer la ley de Dios, y nunca podría obedecerla.

fr.L: Parce que la pensée de la chair [est] hostilité envers Dieu, car elle ne se soumet pas à la Loi de Dieu, et elle ne le peut même pas.
fr.B: En effet, l’orientation de la chair est en guerre contre Dieu. Elle ne se soumet pas à la Loi de Dieu, et en fait elle en est incapable.
fr.R: Notre nature pécheresse est l’ennemie de Dieu. Elle refuse d’obéir à la Loi de Dieu, et elle ne pourrait jamais lui obéir.

sw.L: Kwa sababu fikira za mwili [ni] uadui dhidi ya Mungu, kwa maana haziitii sheria ya Mungu, wala kwa kweli haziwezi.
sw.B: Hii ni kwa sababu mtazamo wa asili ya dhambi uko vitani na Mungu. Hautii sheria ya Mungu, na kwa kweli hauwezi kuitii.
sw.R: Asili ya dhambi ni adui wa Mungu. Inakataa kutii sheria ya Mungu, na haingeweza kamwe kuitii.

decisions.choice: hostility: enmity, being an enemy
decisions.reason: echthra is the state of enemies at war. Paul has said that we were God's enemies before he reconciled us (5:10).

decisions.choice: the subject of "does not submit" and "is not able" is the mindset of the flesh
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular and continue from "the mindset of the flesh". Paul is not saying that people cannot ever turn to God; he says that the flesh, as such, will never submit to God's law.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway
decisions.reason: In Romans 7-8 the flesh is human life in its weakness, under sin's sway and set against God's Spirit (7:5, 7:18, 7:25; Galatians 5:16-17). Paul does not mean the body as such, which God will give life to (verse 11).

decisions.choice: is at war with God (B); is God's enemy (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the strength of the word for enmity (m1).

decisions.choice: the sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means (m3).

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.

records.literal_gloss: The [ones] and in flesh being God to please not are able.

en.L: And those who are in [the] flesh are not able to please God.
en.B: People who are in the flesh have no power to please God.
en.R: People who are ruled by their sinful selves cannot do what pleases God.

es.L: Y los que están en [la] carne no son capaces de agradar a Dios.
es.B: Los que están en la carne no tienen poder para agradar a Dios.
es.R: Las personas dominadas por su yo pecador no pueden hacer lo que agrada a Dios.

fr.L: Et ceux qui sont dans la chair ne peuvent pas plaire à Dieu.
fr.B: Les gens qui sont dans la chair n’ont pas le pouvoir de plaire à Dieu.
fr.R: Les gens que domine leur nature pécheresse ne peuvent pas faire ce qui plaît à Dieu.

sw.L: Na wale walio katika mwili hawawezi kumpendeza Mungu.
sw.B: Watu walio chini ya utawala wa asili ya dhambi hawana uwezo wa kumpendeza Mungu.
sw.R: Watu wanaotawaliwa na asili yao ya dhambi hawawezi kufanya yale yanayompendeza Mungu.

decisions.choice: in the flesh: in the old state ruled by sin
decisions.reason: Paul said "when we were in the flesh" of the life before Christ (7:5). He still lives in a body (Galatians 2:20), so "in the flesh" here is the state of life ruled by sin, not having a body.

decisions.choice: please God: be acceptable to him, do what he approves
decisions.reason: areskō is to please someone, to win their approval, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:1.

decisions.choice: ruled by their sinful selves
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the flesh" means (m1).

source.text: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: You but not are in flesh but in Spirit, if indeed Spirit of God dwells in you.

en.L: But you are not in [the] flesh but in [the] Spirit, if indeed [the] Spirit of God dwells in you.
en.B: But you are not in the flesh; you are in the Spirit, if God's Spirit really does live in you.
en.R: But you are not ruled by your sinful selves. The Spirit rules you, if God's Spirit really lives in you.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no están|vosotros no estáis}} en [la] carne sino en [el] Espíritu, si en verdad [el] Espíritu de Dios habita en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no están|vosotros no estáis}} en la carne; {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en el Espíritu, si de verdad el Espíritu de Dios vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Pero a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no {{plural_you:los|os}} domina {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador. El Espíritu {{plural_you:los|os}} gobierna, si de verdad el Espíritu de Dios vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Mais vous, vous n’êtes pas dans la chair mais dans l’Esprit, si du moins [l’]Esprit de Dieu habite en vous.
fr.B: Mais vous, vous n’êtes pas dans la chair ; vous êtes dans l’Esprit, si l’Esprit de Dieu habite vraiment en vous.
fr.R: Mais vous, vous n’êtes pas dominés par votre nature pécheresse. C’est l’Esprit qui vous dirige, si l’Esprit de Dieu habite vraiment en vous.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi hamko katika mwili bali katika Roho, kama kweli Roho wa Mungu anaishi ndani yenu.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi hamko chini ya utawala wa asili ya dhambi; mko chini ya utawala wa Roho, ikiwa kweli Roho wa Mungu amefanya makao ndani yenu.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi hamtawaliwi na asili yenu ya dhambi. Roho ndiye anayewatawala, ikiwa kweli Roho wa Mungu anaishi ndani yenu.

decisions.choice: if indeed: a condition Paul assumes is met, with a gentle check
decisions.reason: eiper ("if indeed") assumes the readers do have the Spirit, while reminding them that this is what being in the Spirit depends on. Paul uses it again in verse 17.

decisions.choice: in the flesh, in the Spirit: two ways of existing, each with its ruling power
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, "in the flesh" is the old life ruled by sin; "in the Spirit" is the new life where God's Spirit lives and rules.

decisions.choice: dwells: lives in, makes a home in
decisions.reason: oikeō is to live in a house. Paul pictures the Spirit at home in the believer, as God dwelt among his people (1 Corinthians 3:16).

decisions.choice: ruled by your sinful selves; the Spirit rules you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two phrases mean (m2).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: The first plural "you" of the chapter. As through Romans, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

source.text: εἰ δέ τις πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει, οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone Spirit of Christ not has, this [one] not is of him.

en.L: But if anyone does not have [the] Spirit of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, this [one] is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.
en.B: If anyone lacks the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, that person is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.
en.R: Anyone who does not have the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is not one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

es.L: Y si alguien no tiene [el] Espíritu {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, este no es {{deity_pronoun:suyo|Suyo}}.
es.B: Si alguien carece del Espíritu {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, esa persona no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pertenece.
es.R: Quien no tiene el Espíritu {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} no es parte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un n’a pas [l’]Esprit du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, celui-là n’est pas à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un n’a pas l’Esprit du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, il ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartient pas.
fr.R: Celui qui n’a pas l’Esprit du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ne fait pas partie de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa mtu yeyote hana Roho wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, huyo si {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Ikiwa mtu hana Roho wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mtu huyo si {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Mtu asiye na Roho wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} si mmoja wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God is the Spirit of Christ
alternatives: a different spirit, such as Christ's attitude
decisions.reason: In one breath Paul calls the same Spirit "the Spirit of God" and "the Spirit of Christ" (verses 9-11), as in Galatians 4:6 ("the Spirit of his Son"). The Spirit belongs to the Father and to the Son.

decisions.choice: his: Christ's
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to Christ, just named: whoever lacks his Spirit does not belong to him.

source.text: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: If but Christ in you, the indeed body dead because of sin, the but Spirit life because of righteousness.

en.L: But if {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] in you, the body [is] dead because of sin, but the Spirit [is] life because of righteousness.
en.B: But if {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is in you, the body is marked for death because of sin, but the Spirit is life for you because of righteousness.
en.R: But if {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} lives in you, your body will still die because of sin. But the Spirit gives you life, because of the righteousness God has given you.

es.L: Pero si {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} [está] en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, el cuerpo [está] muerto debido al pecado, pero el Espíritu [es] vida debido a [la] justicia.
es.B: Pero si {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} está en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, el cuerpo está destinado a la muerte por el pecado, pero el Espíritu es vida para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por la justicia.
es.R: Pero si {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo de todos modos morirá a causa del pecado. Pero el Espíritu {{plural_you:les|os}} da vida, por la justicia que Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado.

fr.L: Mais si le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} [est] en vous, le corps [est] mort à cause du péché, mais l’Esprit [est] vie à cause de la justice.
fr.B: Mais si le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est en vous, le corps est voué à la mort à cause du péché, mais l’Esprit est vie pour vous à cause de la justice.
fr.R: Mais si le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} vit en vous, votre corps mourra quand même à cause du péché. Mais l’Esprit vous donne la vie, à cause de la justice que Dieu vous a donnée.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [yumo] ndani yenu, mwili [ni] mfu kwa sababu ya dhambi, lakini Roho [ni] uzima kwa sababu ya haki.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yuko ndani yenu, mwili umeandikiwa kufa kwa sababu ya dhambi, lakini Roho ni uzima kwenu kwa sababu ya haki.
sw.R: Lakini ikiwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anaishi ndani yenu, miili yenu bado itakufa kwa sababu ya dhambi. Lakini Roho anawapa uzima, kwa sababu ya haki ambayo Mungu amewapa.

decisions.choice: the Spirit, God's Spirit, is life
decisions.reason: pneuma could be the believer's own spirit, alive while the body dies. But Paul writes "life", a noun, not "alive", and in verses 2, 6 and 11 it is God's Spirit who gives life. So the sense is most likely that the Spirit is life for the believer.

decisions.choice: the body is dead: mortal, bound to die because of sin
decisions.reason: Verse 11 calls the same bodies "mortal". Since Adam, death came to all because of sin (5:12), and believers' bodies still die; but God will give them life.

decisions.choice: because of righteousness: God's gift of right standing with him
alternatives: the righteous life the Spirit produces
decisions.reason: In Romans righteousness is above all what God gives in Christ, the right standing of 5:17 and 5:21 ("grace reigning through righteousness to eternal life"). It may include the righteous life that follows (6:18), but the contrast with "because of sin" points to God's verdict.

decisions.choice: Christ in you: the same as the Spirit dwelling in you
decisions.reason: Paul moves from "the Spirit of God dwells in you" to "Christ in you" without a break. Christ lives in believers by his Spirit.

decisions.choice: marked for death
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "dead" means here (m2): the body is bound to die, not already a corpse.

decisions.choice: the righteousness God has given you
decisions.reason: Readable says whose righteousness it is (m3).

decisions.choice: la justice (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets: "justice" is the key word at every level here, and Readable says whose it is (m3), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: umeandikiwa kufa
decisions.reason: The body is not yet dead but bound to die because of sin (m2). "Kuandikiwa" (to be destined) says this as the English Balanced "marked for death" does; Literal keeps the bare adjective "mfu".

source.text: εἰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὁ ἐγείρας ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ζῳοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τὸ ἐνοικοῦν αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: If and the Spirit of the [one] having raised Jesus out of dead dwells in you, the [one] having raised out of dead Christ Jesus will give life also to the mortal bodies of you because of the dwelling of him Spirit in you.

en.L: And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from [the] dead dwells in you, the one who raised {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus from [the] dead will give life also to your mortal bodies because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit who dwells in you.
en.B: And if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead has made a home in you, then God, who raised {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus from the dead, will bring your mortal bodies to life as well, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit lives in you.
en.R: God raised Jesus from death. If God's Spirit lives in you, then God, who raised {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus from death, will also give life to your bodies, which now must die. He will do this because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit lives in you.

es.L: Y si el Espíritu del que resucitó a Jesús de entre [los] muertos habita en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, el que resucitó {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} de entre [los] muertos dará vida también a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuerpos mortales a causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu que habita en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Y si el Espíritu de aquel que resucitó a Jesús de entre los muertos ha hecho morada en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, entonces Dios, que resucitó {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} de entre los muertos, dará vida también a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuerpos mortales, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Dios resucitó a Jesús de la muerte. Si el Espíritu de Dios vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, entonces Dios, que resucitó {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} de la muerte, también dará vida a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cuerpos, que ahora tienen que morir. Lo hará porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu vive en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et si l’Esprit de celui qui a ressuscité Jésus d’entre les morts habite en vous, celui qui a ressuscité le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus d’entre les morts donnera la vie aussi à vos corps mortels à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit qui habite en vous.
fr.B: Et si l’Esprit de celui qui a ressuscité Jésus d’entre les morts a fait sa demeure en vous, alors Dieu, qui a ressuscité le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus d’entre les morts, donnera aussi la vie à vos corps mortels, parce que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit habite en vous.
fr.R: Dieu a ressuscité Jésus d’entre les morts. Si l’Esprit de Dieu habite en vous, alors Dieu, qui a ressuscité le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, donnera aussi la vie à vos corps, qui doivent maintenant mourir. Il le fera parce que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit habite en vous.

sw.L: Na ikiwa Roho wa yule aliyemfufua Yesu kutoka kwa wafu anaishi ndani yenu, yule aliyemfufua {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kutoka kwa wafu ataipa uzima pia miili yenu inayokufa kwa sababu ya Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anayeishi ndani yenu.
sw.B: Na ikiwa Roho wa yule aliyemfufua Yesu kutoka kwa wafu amefanya makao ndani yenu, basi Mungu, aliyemfufua {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kutoka kwa wafu, ataipa uzima pia miili yenu inayokufa, kwa sababu Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anaishi ndani yenu.
sw.R: Mungu alimfufua Yesu kutoka kwa wafu. Ikiwa Roho wa Mungu anaishi ndani yenu, basi Mungu, aliyemfufua {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kutoka kwa wafu, ataipa uzima pia miili yenu, ambayo sasa ni lazima ife. Atafanya hivyo kwa sababu Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anaishi ndani yenu.

decisions.choice: will give life to your mortal bodies: the resurrection of the body
decisions.reason: The verb is future and the object is the mortal body, the body that dies (verse 10). Paul means that God will raise believers as he raised Jesus (6:5, 1 Corinthians 15:22).

decisions.choice: because of his Spirit who dwells in you
alternatives: "through his Spirit who dwells in you"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts are divided between two forms that differ by one ending: "because of his Spirit" (the SBLGNT) and "through his Spirit". The first gives the Spirit's presence as the reason God will raise the body; the second makes the Spirit the one through whom he does it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: the one who raised Jesus: God
decisions.reason: Paul describes God by what he did in raising Jesus, as in 4:24. The verse names the Father, the Son and the Spirit together.

decisions.choice: if: a condition Paul assumes is true of his readers
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Paul speaks of what is true for his readers, while saying what it depends on.

decisions.choice: God, who raised
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, whom the phrase describes (m3).

decisions.choice: God raised Jesus from death; your bodies, which now must die
decisions.reason: Readable states first the fact the condition rests on, then the promise, and explains "mortal".

source.text: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν, οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν, εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνῄσκειν, εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε, ζήσεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: So then, brothers, debtors we are, not to the flesh, of the according to flesh to live, \v 13 if for according to flesh you live, you are about to die; if but by Spirit the deeds of the body you put to death, you will live.

en.L: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to [the] flesh. \v 13 For if you live according to [the] flesh, you are going to die; but if by [the] Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
en.B: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are under an obligation, but not to the flesh, to live as the flesh dictates. \v 13 If you live as the flesh dictates, you are headed for death. But if by the Spirit you keep putting the body's practices to death, you will live.
en.R: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we do owe something, but we owe nothing to our sinful selves. We do not have to live the way they want. \v 13 If you live the way your sinful self wants, you will die. But if, with the Spirit's power, you keep killing off the sinful things you do with your body, you will live.

es.L: Por consiguiente, hermanos, somos deudores, no de la carne, para vivir según [la] carne; \v 13 porque si {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} según [la] carne, {{plural_you:van|vais}} a morir; pero si por [el] Espíritu {{plural_you:dan|dais}} muerte a las prácticas del cuerpo, {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}.
es.B: Así pues, hermanos, tenemos una obligación, pero no con la carne, para vivir como la carne manda. \v 13 Si {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} como la carne manda, {{plural_you:van|vais}} camino de la muerte. Pero si por el Espíritu {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} dando muerte a las prácticas del cuerpo, {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}.
es.R: Así que, hermanos, sí tenemos una deuda, pero no le debemos nada a nuestro yo pecador. No tenemos que vivir como él quiere. \v 13 Si {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} como quiere {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador, {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}. Pero si, con el poder del Espíritu, {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} acabando con lo malo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} con {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo, {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous sommes débiteurs, non envers la chair, pour vivre selon la chair. \v 13 Car si vous vivez selon la chair, vous allez mourir ; mais si par l’Esprit vous faites mourir les actions du corps, vous vivrez.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous avons une obligation, mais pas envers la chair, pour vivre comme elle l’exige. \v 13 Si vous vivez comme la chair l’exige, vous allez vers la mort. Mais si, par l’Esprit, vous continuez de faire mourir les pratiques du corps, vous vivrez.
fr.R: Ainsi, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous avons bien une dette, mais nous ne devons rien à notre nature pécheresse. Nous ne sommes pas obligés de vivre comme elle le veut. \v 13 Si vous vivez comme le veut votre nature pécheresse, vous mourrez. Mais si, avec la force de l’Esprit, vous continuez à détruire le mal que vous faites avec votre corps, vous vivrez.

sw.L: Basi, ndugu, sisi ni wadaiwa, si wa mwili, ili tuishi kwa kadiri ya mwili; \v 13 kwa maana mkiishi kwa kadiri ya mwili, mnaelekea kufa; lakini kwa Roho mkiyaua matendo ya mwili, mtaishi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, ndugu, tunadaiwa, lakini si na asili ya dhambi, ili tuishi kama inavyotuamuru. \v 13 Mkiishi kama asili ya dhambi inavyoamuru, mnaelekea kifo. Lakini kwa Roho mkiendelea kuyaua matendo ya mwili, mtaishi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu, tunadaiwa kitu, lakini hatudaiwi chochote na asili yetu ya dhambi. Hatulazimiki kuishi jinsi inavyotaka. \v 13 Mkiishi jinsi asili yenu ya dhambi inavyotaka, mtakufa. Lakini kwa nguvu ya Roho mkiendelea kuyakomesha mambo maovu mnayoyatenda kwa miili yenu, mtaishi.

decisions.choice: we are debtors, not to the flesh: the debt is owed to God's Spirit, though Paul does not finish the thought
decisions.reason: Paul says only to whom we owe nothing. The rest of the sentence, and verses 2-11, show that what believers owe is to live by the Spirit who gives them life.

decisions.choice: flesh: human nature under sin's sway, set against the Spirit
decisions.reason: As in verses 3-9, the flesh is human life ruled by sin and opposed to the Spirit, not the body as such.

decisions.choice: you are going to die: death as the end of that way of life, cut off from God
alternatives: only bodily death, which comes to all
decisions.reason: Everyone dies in the body, including those who live by the Spirit (verse 10). The contrast with "you will live", the life of verses 6 and 11, shows that Paul means death in the full sense, the wages of sin (6:23).

decisions.choice: the deeds of the body: sinful practices carried out through the body
decisions.reason: Paul has spoken of sin reigning in the mortal body and using its members (6:12-13). The "deeds of the body" are what the body does under that rule; the body itself is not evil.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit you put to death: the Spirit is the power, and the killing goes on
decisions.reason: The dative "by the Spirit" gives the means: believers do this in the Spirit's strength, not their own. The present tense of the verb points to something done again and again, not once for all.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: Paul addresses the whole church in Rome as members of one family, as in 1:13 and 7:1; the plural includes the sisters.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive default names everyone Paul addresses (m6); the traditional setting keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: keep putting to death (B); keep killing off (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the ongoing action of the present tense (m5).

decisions.choice: the sinful things you do with your body; your sinful self
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the deeds of the body" (m4) and "flesh" (m2) mean here.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:13 and 12:1, Spanish "hermanos" already includes the sisters (m6), so there is no gender span here or in verse 29.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:13 and 12:1, "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters (m6), so Swahili needs no gender span here or in verse 29.

decisions.choice: matendo ya mwili (L, B); mambo maovu mnayoyatenda kwa miili yenu (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Greek word is the body, not the flesh: sinful practices carried out through the body (m4). So every level says "mwili" or "miili", and "asili ya dhambi" is kept for the flesh in verses 12-13a.

source.text: ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: As many as for by Spirit of God are led, these sons are of God.

en.L: For as many as are led by [the] Spirit of God, these are {{gender:children|sons}} of God.
en.B: Those whom God's Spirit is leading are God's {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.R: All the people God's Spirit leads are God's own {{gender:children|sons}}.

es.L: Porque todos aquellos a quienes guía [el] Espíritu de Dios, esos son hijos de Dios.
es.B: Aquellos a quienes el Espíritu de Dios va guiando son hijos de Dios.
es.R: Todas las personas que el Espíritu de Dios guía son los propios hijos de Dios.

fr.L: Car tous ceux qui sont conduits par l’Esprit de Dieu, ceux-là sont {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.
fr.B: Ceux que l’Esprit de Dieu conduit sont {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.
fr.R: Tous ceux que l’Esprit de Dieu conduit sont les propres {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.

sw.L: Kwa maana wote ambao Roho wa Mungu huwaongoza, hawa ni wana wa Mungu.
sw.B: Wale ambao Roho wa Mungu anawaongoza siku kwa siku, hao ndio wana wa Mungu.
sw.R: Watu wote ambao Roho wa Mungu anawaongoza ni wana halisi wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: sons: the standing of a son and heir, given to women and men alike
decisions.reason: huios is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir. Paul gives that standing to every believer, women and men alike (Galatians 3:26-29), and in verses 16-17 he says the same with the word for children, which has no gender.

decisions.choice: led: guided day by day
decisions.reason: agō is to lead or guide. The present tense describes the Spirit's ongoing direction of a believer's life, the life of putting sin to death in verse 13 (compare Galatians 5:18).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word gives the standing of a son and heir (m1), which Paul gives to men and women alike. The inclusive default says who has it; the traditional setting keeps "sons", which shows the standing more plainly.

decisions.choice: hijos, no setting
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "children" with "sons" as the traditional form, Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters and keeps the standing of a son and heir (m1), as in Galatians 3:26 and 4:5. So verses 14, 15, 19 and 23 have no gender span.

decisions.choice: a quienes guía [el] Espíritu de Dios
alternatives: los que son guiados por el Espíritu de Dios
decisions.reason: The Greek passive is turned into an active verb with the Spirit as subject; the sense is the same, and the familiar passive wording is avoided.

decisions.choice: {{gender:enfants|fils}} (also 8:15, 8:19, 8:23)
decisions.reason: As in English, the inclusive default says who has the standing of son and heir (m1), and the traditional setting keeps "fils". "Enfants" and "fils" are both masculine plural, so nothing around the noun changes. In 8:16-17 and 8:21 the Greek has the word for children, and French writes "enfants" with no span.

decisions.choice: wana, no setting
decisions.reason: "Wana" is used of sons and daughters alike and keeps the heir's standing (m1), as in Galatians 3:26 and 4:5; "watoto" would lose it and is kept for the other word for children in verses 16, 17 and 21. So verses 14, 15, 19 and 23 have no gender span.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ·

records.literal_gloss: Not for you received a spirit of slavery again to fear, but you received Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry: Abba, the Father;

en.L: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery [bringing you] back into fear, but you received [the] Spirit of adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father!"
en.B: What you received was not a spirit of slavery that would put you back under fear. You received the Spirit of adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}, and in the Spirit we call out, "Abba, Father!"
en.R: When God gave you the Spirit, God did not make you slaves again, living in fear. By giving you the Spirit, God gave you adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}. And by the Spirit we cry out to God, "Abba! Father!"

es.L: Porque no {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} un espíritu de esclavitud [que {{plural_you:los|os}} lleve] otra vez al temor, sino que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} [el] Espíritu de adopción como hijos, mediante el cual clamamos: «¡Abba, Padre!»
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} no fue un espíritu de esclavitud que {{plural_you:los|os}} volviera a someter al miedo. {{plural_you:Recibieron|Recibisteis}} el Espíritu de adopción como hijos, y en el Espíritu clamamos: «¡Abba, Padre!»
es.R: Cuando Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dio el Espíritu, no {{plural_you:los|os}} hizo esclavos otra vez, para vivir con miedo. Con el Espíritu, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} adoptó como hijos. Y por el Espíritu clamamos a Dios: «¡Abba! ¡Padre!»

fr.L: Car vous n’avez pas reçu un esprit d’esclavage [pour retomber] dans la crainte, mais vous avez reçu [l’]Esprit d’adoption comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}, par lequel nous crions : « Abba, Père ! »
fr.B: Ce que vous avez reçu, ce n’est pas un esprit d’esclavage qui vous ferait retomber dans la peur. Vous avez reçu l’Esprit qui fait de vous des {{gender:enfants|fils}} adoptifs, et c’est par l’Esprit que nous crions : « Abba, Père ! »
fr.R: Quand Dieu vous a donné l’Esprit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne vous a pas rendus de nouveau esclaves, pour vivre dans la peur. En vous donnant l’Esprit, Dieu vous a adoptés comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}. Et par l’Esprit, nous crions à Dieu : « Abba ! Père ! »

sw.L: Kwa maana hamkupokea roho ya utumwa [iwarudishe] tena katika hofu, bali mlimpokea Roho wa kufanywa wana; kwa huyo tunalia, "Aba, Baba!"
sw.B: Hamkupokea roho ya utumwa ambayo ingewarudisha tena chini ya hofu. Mlimpokea Roho wa kufanywa wana, na katika Roho tunaita, "Aba, Baba!"
sw.R: Mungu alipowapa Roho, hakuwafanya watumwa tena wa kuishi kwa hofu. Kwa kuwapa Roho, Mungu aliwafanya wana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Na kwa Roho tunamlilia Mungu, "Aba! Baba!"

decisions.choice: a spirit of slavery: the Spirit they received is not one who enslaves
decisions.reason: Paul is not saying that they received a spirit of slavery before. He sets the Spirit they did receive against what that Spirit is not: one who would make them slaves again, as they were under sin (6:17-20). The lowercase shows that the phrase names what the Spirit is not.

decisions.choice: adoption as sons: being made a son and heir by law
alternatives: the feeling of being God's children
decisions.reason: huiothesia is the legal word for adoption. In Roman law an adopted son received the full rights of a son born into the family, including the inheritance (verse 17). Paul gives that standing to every believer, women as much as men (Galatians 4:5-7).

decisions.choice: Abba: the Aramaic word for "father", followed by the Greek word
decisions.reason: Abba is the Aramaic word a child used for a father, and the word Jesus used in his own prayer (Mark 14:36). The churches kept the Aramaic word and added its translation, as Galatians 4:6 also does. Believers address God the way the Son does.

decisions.choice: by whom we cry: in the Spirit's power we call God Father
alternatives: a new sentence beginning "By him we cry", leading into verse 16
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation joins "in whom we cry" to the Spirit of adoption. krazō is to cry out aloud, here in prayer. In Galatians 4:6 it is the Spirit who cries; here "we" do, by the Spirit.

decisions.choice: from "you" to "we"
decisions.reason: Paul says "you received" and then "we cry": he and his readers pray in the same way, Jew and Gentile alike.

decisions.choice: adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word gives the standing of a son and heir (m2), which Paul gives to men and women alike. The inclusive default says who is adopted; the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: God gave you the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver, God, so the sentence can say plainly what he did and did not do.

decisions.choice: «¡Abba, Padre!» (L, B); «¡Abba! ¡Padre!» (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is kept, followed by "Padre" as the Greek gives its translation (m3), as in Galatians 4:6. "Adopción como hijos" has no gender setting (see verse 14).

decisions.choice: roho ya utumwa (lowercase, class 9); Roho wa kufanywa wana (personal agreement); Aba, Baba
decisions.reason: The spirit of slavery is not a spirit they received (m1), so it is written lowercase with the agreement of a thing ("roho ya utumwa ... ingewarudisha"), while God's Spirit takes personal agreement ("mlimpokea Roho wa"). The Aramaic word is written "Aba", as in Galatians 4:6, since Swahili spelling does not double consonants. "Kufanywa wana" has no gender setting (see verse 14).

decisions.choice: slave(s), slavery
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: a spirit of slavery set against the Spirit of adoption as children.

source.text: αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Itself the Spirit bears witness with the spirit of us that we are children of God.

en.L: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God.
en.B: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} joins our own spirit in testifying that we are God's children.
en.R: The Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} agrees with what our own spirit says: we are God's children.

es.L: El Espíritu mismo atestigua juntamente con nuestro espíritu que somos hijos de Dios.
es.B: El Espíritu mismo se une a nuestro propio espíritu para declarar que somos hijos de Dios.
es.R: El Espíritu mismo confirma lo que dice nuestro propio espíritu: somos hijos de Dios.

fr.L: L’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} rend témoignage avec notre esprit que nous sommes enfants de Dieu.
fr.B: L’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} se joint à notre propre esprit pour témoigner que nous sommes enfants de Dieu.
fr.R: L’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est d’accord avec ce que dit notre propre esprit : nous sommes les enfants de Dieu.

sw.L: Roho {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} anashuhudia sambamba na roho yetu ya kuwa sisi ni watoto wa Mungu.
sw.B: Roho {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} anaungana na roho yetu katika kutoa ushahidi kwamba sisi ni watoto wa Mungu.
sw.R: Roho {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} anakubaliana na kile ambacho roho yetu inasema: sisi ni watoto wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: our spirit: the believer's own human spirit
decisions.reason: Paul sets "the Spirit himself" beside "our spirit", so the second is the human spirit, the inner self that prays "Abba" (verse 15).

decisions.choice: bears witness with: two witnesses agree
decisions.reason: summartureō is to testify together with someone. The Spirit adds his witness to that of our spirit, so that two witnesses confirm the matter, as the law required (Deuteronomy 19:15). Some read it as the Spirit testifying to our spirit; the word itself means "with".

decisions.choice: children: the word for children, of either sex
decisions.reason: teknon has no gender. Paul moves from "sons" (verse 14) to "children" without changing the sense: those who belong to God's family.

decisions.choice: the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is neuter only because the word for spirit is neuter. The Spirit is a person who testifies, prays and searches, so he is never called "it".

decisions.choice: el Espíritu mismo, no setting; nuestro espíritu (lowercase); hijos
decisions.reason: The Spirit is never "it": Spanish says "el Espíritu mismo", which is masculine like the noun. "Mismo" is an intensifier, not a pronoun, so it takes no deity_pronoun span, unlike the English "himself". "Our spirit" is the believer's own human spirit (m1) and is written lowercase. Spanish has only "hijos" for the word for children here (m3), the same word it uses for "sons" in verses 14-15; the difference cannot be shown.

decisions.choice: Roho {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; roho yetu (lowercase, class 9); watoto
decisions.reason: "Mwenyewe" is a free pronoun, the kind the deity_pronoun setting applies to in Swahili, so it carries the span as the English "himself" does; God's Spirit takes personal agreement ("anashuhudia"). The human spirit (m1) is written lowercase with the agreement of a thing ("roho yetu ... inasema"), which keeps the two apart. The word for children here is "watoto" (m3), not "wana" as in verses 14-15.

source.text: εἰ δὲ τέκνα, καὶ κληρονόμοι· κληρονόμοι μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ, εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν.

records.literal_gloss: If and children, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, joint-heirs and of Christ, if indeed we suffer with [him] so that also we may be glorified with [him].

en.L: And if children, also heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, if indeed we suffer with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] so that we may also be glorified with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
en.B: If we are children, we are also heirs. We are God's heirs, and we inherit alongside {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, if we suffer together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that we will also be glorified together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: And because we are God's children, we will receive everything God has promised to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children. We will receive it together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. But we must suffer with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} now, so that we will also share {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory later.

es.L: Y si [somos] hijos, también [somos] herederos: herederos de Dios, y coherederos junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, si de veras sufrimos con [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] para que también seamos glorificados con [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}].
es.B: Si somos hijos, también somos herederos. Somos herederos de Dios, y heredamos junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, si sufrimos junto con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para ser también glorificados junto con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Y como somos hijos de Dios, recibiremos todo lo que Dios ha prometido dar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos. Lo recibiremos junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Pero ahora tenemos que sufrir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, para que después también compartamos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria.

fr.L: Et si [nous sommes] enfants, [nous sommes] aussi héritiers : héritiers de Dieu et cohéritiers du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, si du moins nous souffrons avec [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] afin d’être aussi glorifiés avec [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}].
fr.B: Si nous sommes enfants, nous sommes aussi héritiers. Nous sommes héritiers de Dieu, et nous recevons l’héritage avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, si nous souffrons avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour être aussi glorifiés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Et puisque nous sommes les enfants de Dieu, nous recevrons tout ce que Dieu a promis de donner à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants. Nous recevrons tout cela avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Mais nous devons souffrir avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} maintenant, pour avoir aussi part à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire plus tard.

sw.L: Na ikiwa [ni] watoto, basi [ni] warithi pia: warithi wa Mungu na warithi wenza wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ikiwa kweli tunateseka pamoja [na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}] ili tutukuzwe pia pamoja [na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}].
sw.B: Ikiwa sisi ni watoto, basi sisi ni warithi pia. Sisi ni warithi wa Mungu, na tunarithi pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ikiwa tunateseka pamoja naye ili tutukuzwe pia pamoja naye.
sw.R: Na kwa kuwa sisi ni watoto wa Mungu, tutapokea kila kitu ambacho Mungu ameahidi kuwapa watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Tutakipokea pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Lakini sasa ni lazima tuteseke pamoja naye, ili baadaye tushiriki pia utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: heirs: those who will receive the inheritance
decisions.reason: Children inherit from their father. The inheritance God promised Abraham was the world (4:13); for believers it is the coming glory of verse 18 and the renewed creation of verse 21.

decisions.choice: if indeed we suffer with him: suffering with Christ is part of belonging to him
alternatives: a doubt whether they will suffer
decisions.reason: eiper (as in verse 9) states a condition Paul expects to be met. Those who share Christ's inheritance share his path, through suffering to glory.

decisions.choice: so that we may also be glorified with him: suffering leads to glory
decisions.reason: hina gives the purpose and goal: suffering with Christ is the road to sharing his glory, as verse 18 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: we will receive everything God has promised; share his glory later
decisions.reason: Readable explains what being an heir means (m1) and what being glorified with Christ means.

decisions.choice: pamoja naye, no span (B, R); [pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}] (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "naye", where the pronoun is joined to the conjunction and cannot take a capital, so there is no span where the English has "him". Literal brackets the supplied "with him" and writes the free pronoun "yeye", which takes the span.

source.text: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: I reckon for that not worthy the sufferings of the now time toward the about-to-be glory to be revealed to us.

en.L: For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time [are] not worthy [to be set] against the coming glory to be revealed to us.
en.B: I have weighed it up: what we suffer in this present time does not begin to balance the glory that is going to be revealed to us.
en.R: We suffer now. But I am sure that our suffering is very small next to the glory God will show us in the future.

es.L: Porque estimo que los sufrimientos del tiempo actual no [son] de peso [comparados] con la gloria que va a ser revelada a nosotros.
es.B: Lo he pensado bien: lo que sufrimos en este tiempo presente ni siquiera empieza a igualar en peso la gloria que se nos va a revelar.
es.R: Ahora sufrimos. Pero estoy seguro de que nuestro sufrimiento es muy poca cosa al lado de la gloria que Dios nos mostrará en el futuro.

fr.L: Car je compte que les souffrances du temps présent ne [sont] pas dignes [d’être mises en balance] avec la gloire qui va être révélée envers nous.
fr.B: J’ai bien pesé la chose : ce que nous souffrons dans le temps présent est loin de faire le poids face à la gloire qui va nous être révélée.
fr.R: Nous souffrons maintenant. Mais je suis sûr que nos souffrances sont toutes petites à côté de la gloire que Dieu nous montrera plus tard.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninaona kwamba mateso ya wakati uliopo [hayastahili] kulinganishwa na utukufu ujao utakaodhihirishwa kwetu.
sw.B: Nimelipima jambo hili: tunayoteseka katika wakati huu uliopo hayakaribii hata kidogo uzito wa utukufu utakaofunuliwa kwetu.
sw.R: Sasa tunateseka. Lakini nina hakika kwamba mateso yetu ni madogo sana ukilinganisha na utukufu ambao Mungu atatuonyesha baadaye.

decisions.choice: not worthy: not of equal weight
decisions.reason: axios first meant "of equal weight" on a pair of scales. Set beside the coming glory, present sufferings weigh almost nothing (2 Corinthians 4:17).

decisions.choice: I reckon: I have thought it through and conclude
decisions.reason: logizomai is a word for careful reckoning, the same word as "counted" in chapter 4. Paul states a settled judgment.

decisions.choice: revealed to us: shown to us and given to us
decisions.reason: eis can mean "to", "toward" or "upon". The glory will be shown to believers and they will share it (verse 17); the passive leaves God as the one who reveals it.

decisions.choice: the present time: the time between Christ's coming and his return
decisions.reason: Paul calls this "the now time" (3:26, 11:5): already the age of salvation, yet still a time of suffering and waiting (verses 22-25).

decisions.choice: does not begin to balance
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of weighing on scales (m1).

decisions.choice: God will show us
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who reveals the glory (m3).

decisions.choice: est loin de faire le poids face à
decisions.reason: The French idiom keeps the picture of weighing on scales (m1), as the English "does not begin to balance" does.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται·

records.literal_gloss: The for eager expectation of the creation the revelation of the sons of the God awaits;

en.L: For the eager longing of the creation awaits the revelation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of God.
en.B: The created world cranes its neck in longing, waiting for God's {{gender:children|sons}} to be revealed.
en.R: Everything God made is waiting eagerly for the day when God shows who {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}} really are.

es.L: Porque la ansiosa expectación de la creación aguarda la revelación de los hijos de Dios.
es.B: El mundo creado estira el cuello con anhelo, esperando que los hijos de Dios se manifiesten.
es.R: Todo lo que Dios hizo espera con ansias el día en que Dios muestre quiénes son de verdad {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos.

fr.L: Car l’attente ardente de la création attend la révélation des {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu.
fr.B: La création tend le cou dans son ardent désir, attendant que les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu soient révélés.
fr.R: Tout ce que Dieu a fait attend avec impatience le jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montrera qui sont vraiment {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} {{gender:enfants|fils}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana hamu kubwa ya uumbaji inangoja kudhihirishwa kwa wana wa Mungu.
sw.B: Ulimwengu ulioumbwa unanyoosha shingo kwa hamu, ukingoja wana wa Mungu wadhihirishwe.
sw.R: Kila kitu ambacho Mungu aliumba kinangoja kwa hamu siku ambayo Mungu ataonyesha wana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ni akina nani hasa.

decisions.choice: the creation: the world God made, apart from human beings
decisions.reason: ktisis is what God created. Here it groans and waits but did not choose its state (verse 20), and believers are named separately (verse 23), so Paul means the non-human creation, which shares humanity's fall and its hope (Genesis 3:17-18).

decisions.choice: eager longing: watching with head stretched forward
decisions.reason: apokaradokia pictures someone craning the neck to see what is coming. Paul speaks of creation as a person waiting for something it cannot yet see.

decisions.choice: revelation: the moment when God's children are shown for what they are
decisions.reason: Believers are already God's children (verse 16), but this is hidden. At the end it will be made plain, when they share Christ's glory (Colossians 3:4).

decisions.choice: sons: the standing of a son and heir, given to women and men alike
decisions.reason: huios is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir. Paul gives that standing to every believer, women and men alike (Galatians 3:26-29), and in verses 16-17 he says the same with the word for children, which has no gender.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 14: the inclusive default names everyone who has this standing (m4), and the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: cranes its neck in longing
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the word (m2).

decisions.choice: uumbaji (L); ulimwengu ulioumbwa (B)
decisions.reason: The creation here is the world God made, apart from human beings (m1). "Viumbe vyote" (all creatures) would suggest living beings, and people among them; "uumbaji" (creation) and "ulimwengu ulioumbwa" (the created world) name the whole made world, and are kept through verses 19-22.

source.text: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη, οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα, ἐφ’ ἑλπίδι ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: To the for futility the creation was subjected, not willingly but because of the [one] having subjected, in hope \v 21 that also itself the creation will be set free from the slavery of the decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of the God.

en.L: For the creation was subjected to futility, not of its own will but because of the one who subjected [it], in hope \v 21 that the creation itself also will be set free from the slavery of decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
en.B: Creation was made subject to futility. This was not its own choice; it was because of the one who subjected it. Yet there was hope: \v 21 creation itself will also be released from its slavery to decay and will enter the freedom that comes with the glory of God's children.
en.R: Creation was made subject to things that come to nothing. It did not choose this. God made it so, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also gave creation hope. \v 21 One day creation will be set free from decay, which holds it like a slave.
